title: Admin request consolidation and prioritization lifecycle for enterprise access
creator: Aditi Kapoor
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers submit a high volume of admin & access requests (RBAC changes, SSO/SAML integrations, SCIM provisioning rules) via support, sales, and direct PM outreach. Requests are currently routed ad-hoc, causing long response times, duplicated work across teams, and missed compliance steps.

Goal: Build a consolidated lifecycle that classifies incoming admin requests, assigns a risk/effort score, routes to the correct team and SLA, and provides prescriptive resolution paths and audit records. The solution must cover self-serve actions, automated approvals for low-risk changes, and escalations for security-sensitive requests (KMS/HSM, org-wide role changes).

Scope: Non-bug customer requests only (feature/ops requests for access, RBAC policy changes, SSO onboarding, SCIM mappings, org-level policy waivers). This ticket defines the rubric, routing rules, telemetry, and rollout plan; implementation will be split into dependent ENG/DES tickets.
acceptance_criteria: A1: A triage rubric with discrete fields (Request Type, Business Impact, Data Sensitivity, Complexity, Customer Tier, Time Sensitivity) is documented and approved by Security and Support.
A2: Routing matrix defined that maps score ranges to: self-serve guides, identity ops queue, security review, or enterprise engineering intervention.

A3: Example flows and canned response templates for top 6 request types (SSO onboarding, SCIM mapping change, new org-admin request, role creation, cross-org access, emergency rollback) are written and stored in Confluence/Drive.
A4: Telemetry events and dashboard spec for Console are defined (event names, fields, owner) to measure triage latency, resolution time, and re-open rate.
A5: Pilot plan with 3 enterprise customers identified and rollout acceptance criteria recorded.
A6: Security sign-off recorded and checklist items captured before GA.
A7: Linked ENG/DES tickets exist and first implementation sprint is scheduled (dependencies resolved or acknowledged).

runbook_summary: For each incoming admin request, capture standardized fields (type, description, affected org, requester role, requested change, supporting docs). Apply triage rubric to compute score. Route: score <=2 -> self-serve + auto-close with template; 3-5 -> support queue + account manager notification; 6-8 -> identity ops ticket with SLA 72h; 9-10 -> security review + remediation plan; Always attach audit token and request ID.
